source_url: cite: Kurzweil, Ray. The Singularity Is Near: When Humans Transcend Biology. New York: Viking, 2005. Chapter One, The Six Epochs, section The Singularity Is Near
quote: With both the hardware and software needed to fully emulate human intelligence, we can expect computers to pass the Turing test, indicating intelligence indistinguishable from that of biological humans, by the end of the 2020s.
claim_summary: Computers will pass the Turing test, with intelligence indistinguishable from humans, by the end of the 2020s.
definition_note: Turing test pass; intelligence indistinguishable from that of biological humans
notes: timeline_year 2029 read from 'end of the 2020s'. Wording checked against an online text copy of the book on archive.org (item kurzweil-ray-the-singularity-is-near), which looks like an unauthorised upload, so the book is cited rather than linked. Publication month September 2005 from search results, not checked against the publisher.

quote: I set the date for the Singularity—representing a profound and disruptive transformation in human capability—as 2045.
claim_summary: Kurzweil sets 2045 as the date of the Singularity, a profound and disruptive change in human capability.
definition_note: Singularity, not AGI; the same Q&A says 'We'll have both the hardware and software to recreate human intelligence by the end of the 2020s'
notes: Question-and-answer page on the book's official site, undated; the Kurzweil Library reprints the same dialogue (thekurzweillibrary.com/dialogue-a-conversation-on-the-singularity) and says it comes from The Singularity Is Near (2005). source_type interview because it is a question-and-answer format written for the book.

quote: We'll have sufficient hardware to recreate human intelligence pretty soon. We'll have it in a supercomputer by 2010. A thousand dollars of computation will equal the 10,000 trillion calculations per second that I estimate is necessary to emulate the human brain by 2020. The software side will take a little longer.
claim_summary: Hardware able to recreate human intelligence will exist in a supercomputer by 2010 and for $1,000 by 2020; the software will take a little longer.
timeline_text: The software side will take a little longer
definition_note: Hardware able to emulate the human brain (supercomputer by 2010, $1,000 by 2020); a timeline for computing power, not for human-level AI itself
notes: Ubiquity magazine interview (vol. 7 issue 1, 11-17 January 2006), read in the excerpt reposted to the Humanist discussion list; the ACM original (ubiquity.acm.org/article.cfm?id=1117663) returned 403. Speaker's own words in a published interview, so treated as primary.

quote: At the end of the 2020s, we will have both the hardware and software to create human levels of intelligence. This includes emotional intelligence, which is really the cutting edge of intelligence, in a machine.
claim_summary: By the end of the 2020s there will be the hardware and software to create human-level intelligence, including emotional intelligence, in a machine.
definition_note: human levels of intelligence, including emotional intelligence
notes: Interview by Sander Olson, first published on CRNano.org 9 February 2006 and reprinted on KurzweilAI.net 10 February 2006. timeline_year 2029 read from 'end of the 2020s'.

quote: I've made the case that we will have both the hardware and the software to achieve human level artificial intelligence with the broad suppleness of human intelligence including our emotional intelligence by 2029
claim_summary: Human-level AI, with the breadth of human intelligence including emotional intelligence, will be achieved by 2029.
definition_note: human level artificial intelligence with the broad suppleness of human intelligence including emotional intelligence
notes: secondhand; Ubergizmo quoting the BBC story "Machines 'to match man by 2029'" on Kurzweil's talk at the American Association for the Advancement of Science meeting in Boston, February 2008. The BBC original (news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/7248875.stm) could not be fetched, nor its archive.org copy.

quote: For starters, I said that we would be able to reverse-engineer the brain sufficiently to understand its basic principles of operation within two decades, not one decade, as Myers reports.
claim_summary: Kurzweil corrects a reported date: understanding the brain's basic principles of operation will take two decades, not one.
timeline_text: within two decades, not one decade
definition_note: Understanding the brain's principles of operation, which he treats as the route to human-level AI; not AGI itself
notes: computed: 2010 + 20; also: possibility. Reply to biologist PZ Myers's post "Ray Kurzweil does not understand the brain"; corrects a press report of his Singularity Summit 2010 talk. Code judged: the date is for a step toward human-level AI rather than for AGI.

quote: So when a computer does reach human levels, which I believe will happen by the end of the 2020s, it will be able to go out on the Web and read billions of pages as well as have experiences in online virtual worlds.
claim_summary: Replying to Paul Allen's argument that the Singularity is far off, Kurzweil holds that computers will reach human levels by the end of the 2020s.
definition_note: human levels of intelligence; human-level pattern recognition combined with computer speed
notes: also: timeline. Published in Technology Review as "Don't Underestimate the Singularity" (October 2011); the Kurzweil Library copy is dated 20 October 2011. The technologyreview.com URL tried returned 404. Coded possibility because the essay argues the brain is understandable enough to be rebuilt, against Allen; the date is secondary. timeline_year 2029 read from 'end of the 2020s'.

quote: This is about typical for the state of the art in chatbots, and I've seen better.
claim_summary: Kurzweil rejects the claim that the Eugene Goostman chatbot passed the Turing test, calling it typical of current chatbots, while keeping his 2029 date for a valid test.
timeline_text: I specified the 2029 date in my 1999 book
definition_note: valid Turing test: longer than five-minute conversations, no restricted persona such as a 13-year-old non-native speaker
notes: also: timeline. Kurzweil's own post. Stance judged: he dismisses the current claim but remains expectant about a genuine pass by 2029; the same post predicts a period of premature claims that will be debunked.

quote: The median view of AI practitioners today is that we are still several decades from achieving human-level AI. I am more optimistic and put the date at 2029, but either way, we do have time to devise ethical standards.
claim_summary: In an essay arguing AI dangers can be managed, Kurzweil puts human-level AI at 2029, earlier than the median expert view of several decades.
notes: also: timeline. Op-ed by Kurzweil in TIME, "Don't Fear Artificial Intelligence". Coded post_agi because the essay is about managing risk; source_type blog used for a signed opinion piece (no op-ed type in the codebook).

quote: I've stuck with my 2029 prediction, which is now a median view and there is a growing group of people who think I am too conservative.
claim_summary: Kurzweil keeps his 2029 date for human-level machine intelligence, says it is now a median view, and notes many think it too conservative.
timeline_text: I've stuck with my 2029 prediction ... a growing group of people who think I am too conservative
notes: Kurzweil's foreword to Martine Rothblatt's book Virtually Human; the Kurzweil Library dates it 1 March 2016. The book itself may have been published earlier (2014, not checked).

quote: One is 2029, which is when computers will pass a valid Turing test, meaning they'll be indistinguishable from human intelligence in a conversation.
claim_summary: Asked why the Singularity is set for 2045, Kurzweil names 2029 as the year computers pass a valid Turing test.
definition_note: 2029 = valid Turing test pass (indistinguishable from human intelligence in conversation); the same answer explains 2045, the Singularity, as when nonbiological intelligence is a billion times all human intelligence
notes: Playboy interview published 19 April 2016, reprinted in the Kurzweil Library.

quote: 2029 is the consistent date I have predicted for when an AI will pass a valid Turing test and therefore achieve human levels of intelligence. I have set the date 2045 for the 'Singularity' which is when we will multiply our effective intelligence a billion fold by merging with the intelligence we have created.
claim_summary: Kurzweil restates 2029 for a valid Turing test pass and human-level intelligence, and 2045 for the Singularity.
timeline_text: 2029 is the consistent date I have predicted
definition_note: 2029 = valid Turing test pass, which he equates with human levels of intelligence; 2045 = Singularity, multiplying effective intelligence a billion-fold by merging with AI
notes: Statement made "in a communication to Futurism" around SXSW 2017. The Kurzweil Library dates the Futurism story March 2017; the Futurism page shows only 'Updated Oct 16, 2017'.

quote: By 2029, computers will have human-level intelligence.
claim_summary: On stage at SXSW 2017, Kurzweil says computers will have human-level intelligence by 2029.
notes: secondhand; Fox News (16 March 2017) reporting Kurzweil's SXSW session in Austin (interviewers Shira Lazar and Amy Kurzweil). Futurism carries the same quote. No recording or transcript of the session was found; a web search for it could not be run because the search budget ran out.

quote: We're not quite there, but we will be there, and by 2029 it will match any person.
claim_summary: On Joe Rogan's podcast Kurzweil says AI is not yet at human level but will match any person by 2029.
timeline_text: We're not quite there, but we will be there
notes: secondhand; also: capability_now. Business Today (13 March 2024) reporting Joe Rogan Experience episode 2117. archive.org copies of the episode have no transcript or captions; no published transcript found.

quote: Human-level intelligence generally means AI that has reached the ability of the most skilled humans in a particular domain and by 2029 that will be achieved in most respects.
claim_summary: Kurzweil says AI will reach the ability of the most skilled humans in most respects by 2029, perhaps still trailing in a few skills.
timeline_text: by 2029 that will be achieved in most respects
definition_note: ability of the most skilled humans in a particular domain; 'in most respects' by 2029, may still lag top humans in a few skills such as Oscar-winning screenplays or deep new philosophical insights
notes: secondhand; PC Gamer story (8 July 2024, via Yahoo Tech) quoting the Guardian interview of 29 June 2024 (theguardian.com/technology/article/2024/jun/29/ray-kurzweil-google-ai-the-singularity-is-nearer), which the fetch tool could not reach. Hedge: 'in most respects'. Same story quotes 'We're going to expand intelligence a millionfold by 2045'.

quote: But that's now starting to look like a conservative view
claim_summary: Kurzweil says his 2029 date for AGI now starts to look conservative, implying it could come sooner.
timeline_text: now starting to look like a conservative view
definition_note: AGI matching or surpassing human capabilities across a wide range of cognitive tasks (the outlet's wording); same interview: the Singularity is 'where we no longer have control of AI'
notes: BBC Science Focus interview by Alex Hughes. Hedge toward an earlier date. The 2029 date is stated by the outlet in the sentence before the quote. Medium confidence because the definition is the outlet's.

quote: Basically, it will be able to do what an expert in every field can do, all at the same time, and we're not quite there yet, but we will be there by 2029.
claim_summary: Kurzweil defines AGI as doing what an expert in every field can do at once, says it is not here yet, and keeps 2029.
timeline_text: we're not quite there yet, but we will be there by 2029
definition_note: what an expert in every field can do, all at the same time
notes: also: capability_now, definition. TWiT Intelligent Machines episode 810 transcript (0:07:53). Asked whether he wants to adjust the date he said: 'Well, there's no reason for me to adjust it. I mean, I said 2029 in 1999.' (0:11:12). Same episode puts the Singularity, merging with AI, at 2045.
